content:
nina: FYI getting a small but persistent flood of SCIM / SAML failures for several customers after last night's IdP cert + metadata rotation.

nina: Errors look like two patterns: SAML validation/nameid format mismatch and downstream SCIM duplicate ext_id conflicts during provisioning. Raising for triage.

tom: sample SAML response snippet we received from idp.example-cust:```
<Assertion ...>
  <Subject>
    <NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent">abc123-persistent</NameID>
  </Subject>
</Assertion>
```
Previously they sent NameID as an emailAddress format.

maria: We rotated a bunch of customer metadata entries and certificates overnight using the rotation runbook. We did a metadata push window 02:00-02:30 UTC. I confirmed the XML fingerprints matched the uploaded metadata for idp.example-cust when I pushed.

devon: Can you paste the exact errors from the provisioner/service? Also which customers? Is this affecting user logins or only SCIM flows?

nina: Two specific logs:```
2026-04-10T02:41:12Z ERROR saml-assertion svc=auth nameid=abc123 reason=InvalidNameIDFormat expected=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress got=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent
2026-04-10T02:42:05Z ERROR scim-provisioner svc=provisioner userKey=uid=svc-ops-42 status=409 reason=ext_id_conflict existing=uid=svc-ops-42:newid incoming=uid=svc-ops-42:oldemail@example.com
```
Both errors are for the same customer in eu-central-1. A few customers show only the NameID mismatch.

jake: Thought: the IdP rotation changed their NameID format to persistent IDs (maybe they switched a setting). Our SCIM pipeline historically used externalId=emailAddress and lowercased it for uniqueness. If a NameID now contains a stable but opaque id we end up trying to create a new user record whose externalId collides with a different canonicalization rule. That explains the 409s.

maria: Do we have a quick mitigation? Some customers require immediate deprovisioning compliance.

devon: Short-term mitigations: (A) accept both NameID formats in SAML validation for that customer's metadata until they switch back, (B) update SCIM reconciliation to allow mapping from either ext_id or NameID, (C) coordinate with customer to switch NameID to emailAddress if their directory supports it. Option A is fastest.

idp-bot: metadata-bot: metadata-update idp.example-cust applied by @maria at 2026-04-10T02:15Z (cert rotated).

nina: I can contact customer SRE to ask if they intentionally toggled NameID format. If they did, we should add a graceful migration path.

jake: For the SCIM side we can implement a temporary fallback: when provisioning fails with ext_id_conflict, try two lookups: externalId and nameID. Pseudocode:```
user = find_by_external_id(ext) || find_by_nameid(nameid)
if user and user.id != incoming.id -> attach alias mapping and allow reconcile
```
Doable as a hotfix in the provisioner w/ feature flag for 48h.

security-oncall: Keep in mind for compliance we must log any relaxed matching rules and the reason. Mark this as a compliance-impacting change and preserve the original metadata and approval trail.

devon: I'll open infra/roles-hotfix PR for the provisioner change behind a flag. We should scope the flag per-tenant (only affected customers).

maria: Customer SRE responded: they intentionally flipped to persistent NameID to comply with their internal lifecycle; they will not revert. They asked us to accept the persistent IDs as authoritative.

jake: Ok then medium-term plan: update our SCIM canonicalization to treat NameID persistent tokens as a first-class external identifier for provisioning (add to identity model), and add migration backfill job to reconcile accounts that split. Backfill approach: map old email externalId -> new nameid and merge aliases.

nina: BE careful: some customers inflate uniqueness of persistent NameIDs across environments. We need to namespace them by IdP issuer to avoid cross-tenant collisions.

security-oncall: Create ticket SEC-2404: "NameID format migration: support persistent NameID + SCIM alias mapping". Owners: @jake (impl), @devon (deploy), @maria (customer coord), @nina (tests). Add audit log requirement and per-tenant opt-in flag.

maria: I'll schedule a short cross-team call in 20 minutes with customer SRE + prod-identity team to align on contract.

devon: Quick checklist for the hotfix rollout: 1) feature flag per-tenant; 2) log both ext_id and nameid lookup attempts; 3) populate alias table for backfill; 4) add unit tests for nameid/email canonicalization.

jake: I'll start the backfill job design and a migration DB migration to store aliases. Estimate ~3 hours to implement and roll to staging.

nina: Any CVE/vuln implications? The only concern is widened matching logic causing account takeover if misapplied. Make sure the per-tenant flag is enforced and verify issuer claim in assertion before any aliasing.

security-oncall: Agreed. Add security checklist to SEC-2404: issuer validation, signed assertion verification, restrict alias merge to same issuer, require audit trail.

maria: Noted. We'll keep this P2 for now. Will update after the call. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
